tex_content.label: eq:ramp-comparison
tex_content.source:
\begin{equation}
 r\leq L_0,\quad
 \text{turning of each first-boundary subarc of length at most }r<1/200
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \tfrac34L_0\leq L_1.
 \label{eq:ramp-comparison}
\end{equation}
The threshold precedes the circumference, time, and curves.
The ramp degree here need not be one.
\source{MT2007}\dcref{Lemma 19.31, pp. 462, 464--466}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:intrinsic-annular} with
$\delta'=7/800$, $r'=r/4$, and $K=K_0$, obtaining $\mu'$,
and take $\mu=\mu'/2$. If the desired inequality fails by a
gap $d>0$, smooth the labels and separate them in an auxiliary
circle with error below $\min\{\mu'/4,d/4\}$.

The separated minimum is smooth inside and $C^2$ up to its
regular boundary traces. Trim into its interior; the induced
metric is a smooth intrinsic annulus, its Gaussian curvature
is at most $K_0$ by the minimal-surface Gauss equation, and its
area is below $\mu'$. Its first-boundary turning remains below
$7/800$ on arcs of length $r/4$. Apply the intrinsic comparison,
then let the trim and smoothing error vanish, contradicting the gap.
\end{proof}
